record.paper_title: Open problems in membrane computing and how not to solve them
record.original_question: For active-membrane P systems, what is the relationship between computational power obtained by allowing non-confluence and computational power obtained by using deep membrane structures? The setting is that shallow membrane structures can still perform exponentially many parallel computations but collect results in the outermost membrane, deep structures combine results hierarchically, and known shallow non-confluent systems can achieve PSPACE power.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider P systems with active membranes, a model of distributed parallel computation in which objects (multisets of symbols) reside inside a hierarchically nested structure of membranes and evolve in parallel by means of local rewriting and communication rules (object evolution, send-in, send-out, dissolution, and membrane division). The depth of a P system is the maximum nesting depth of its membrane structure; a system is called shallow when this depth equals 1 (a skin membrane containing only elementary membranes), and deep otherwise. A P system is confluent if every nondeterministic computation on a given input yields the same accept/reject answer, and non-confluent otherwise. A recognizer P system family decides a language in polynomial time if there is a uniform polynomial-time construction of systems whose computations halt in polynomial time and correctly decide membership.

It is known that:
(i) polynomial-time uniform families of shallow non-confluent recognizer P systems with active membranes can decide exactly the languages in PSPACE;
(ii) deep membrane structures provide hierarchical combination of results, while shallow systems with exponentially many parallel sub-computations can only collect their outcomes in the outermost membrane.

Determine the precise relationship between the computational power gained from allowing non-confluence and the computational power gained from increasing membrane depth in polynomial-time uniform families of recognizer P systems with active membranes. In particular, characterize the class of languages decided by deep confluent P systems with active membranes in polynomial time, and compare it to PSPACE and to the classes obtained by combining or separating these two features (depth versus non-confluence).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent results (2019, Journal of Membrane Computing) characterize PSPACE via shallow non-confluent P systems, and subsequent work (2020–2022) continues to study space and depth bounds, but the precise comparison between the power afforded by non-confluence and that afforded by membrane depth remains an active open question. No source establishes the full equivalence or separation.

status_evidence.title: Characterizing PSPACE with shallow non-confluent P systems
status_evidence.snippet: shallow polynomial-time non-confluent P systems with depth 1 already suffice for reaching PSPACE
status_evidence.claim: Shallow non-confluent systems characterize PSPACE, motivating the comparison with depth.

status_evidence.title: Bounding the space in P systems with active membranes
status_evidence.snippet: continued investigation of space/depth bounds in P systems with active membranes
status_evidence.claim: Depth-versus-non-confluence trade-offs are still being investigated.

status_evidence.title: Evaluating space measures in P systems
status_evidence.claim: The relationship between depth and non-confluence in P systems remains a topic of ongoing research.
